comparison: Perfect claim overlap (C23-24, C41-51, C99-100) on movement analysis. OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with appropriate controls and validation. Peer reviewers also find SUPPORTED, noting rigorous methods for identifying movement-related neurons, though broader statistical concerns about independence apply. Strong agreement on this aspect of the study.

Perfect claim overlap (C52-57, C71) on dLight photometry data. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with caveat about sensor assumptions. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN due to significant ceiling effect concerns - questioning whether maximal sensor response on first injection could mask actual dopamine increases. Major disagreement on interpretation confidence.

Perfect claim overlap (C4, C25, C58, C60-68, C72-73, C76-77) on SL327 manipulation. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical analyses. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, noting lack of direct comparison to untreated controls and that evidence for D1 neuron role is indirect - SL327 effects could relate to other mechanisms. Significant disagreement on strength of causal evidence.

High claim overlap (C2, C21, C28-29, C31) on acute cocaine effects. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistics and controls. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, raising concerns about lack of direct statistical comparison between D1R and D2R populations, non-independence of neurons from same animal, and fundamental questions about epifluorescence ability to measure individual neurons. Major methodological disagreement.

Moderate claim overlap (C32-38) on neuron tracking methodology. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate cell registration and statistics. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, questioning fundamental methodology of using epifluorescence to assign calcium activity to individual neurons and noting strange morphologies in figures. Significant disagreement on technical validity.

Moderate claim overlap (C3, C22, C39, C69-70) on longitudinal tracking and recruitment findings. OpenEval finds SUPPORTED with appropriate statistical analyses. Peer reviewers rate UNCERTAIN, emphasizing that analyses assume independence when neurons from same animal are not independent, recommending mixed/repeated measures ANOVAs instead. Disagreement on statistical approach adequacy.
OpenEval evaluated literature context claims (C1, C6-20, C40) as SUPPORTED with appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background/contextual claims.

OpenEval evaluated integrative conclusions (C5, C81) as SUPPORTED but noted 'sufficiency' claim is overstated - data show necessity/correlation but not true sufficiency. No corresponding specific peer review evaluation found, though peer concerns about SL327 interpretation (R6) indirectly relate.

OpenEval evaluated mechanistic model claims (C30, C78-80) as SUPPORTED but noted these are inferences rather than directly demonstrated mechanisms. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these mechanistic integration claims.

OpenEval evaluated literature comparison claims (C74-75, C82-86) as SUPPORTED, noting appropriate citations and contextual interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these discussion/comparison claims.

OpenEval evaluated D2R SPN mechanism claims (C88-98) as UNCERTAIN, noting largely speculative mechanistic explanations not directly tested. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific D2R mechanism discussions.

OpenEval evaluated future directions and broader implications (C87, C101-103) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are explicitly speculative hypotheses lacking direct experimental support. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these speculative claims.
